notes.text: Midrash Tehillim and Yalkut Shoftim read R. Yoḥanan, governor of the capital, in this exchange. Heilprin reports Yonatan of Kevurah.
Shabbat 85a:2 names R. Yonatan in the checked Bavli. Shabbat 150a:12 reads Naḥmani with R. Yoḥanan. Heilprin’s list and his printed correction Nahmami have been preserved.
The checked Midrash preserves Shimon bar Naḥmani and names Ḥama bar R. Ḥanina, while Heilprin reports Ḥanina bar Ḥama. His suggested replacement of Shimon with Shmuel remains an emendation.
London Yuhasin, p. 193, includes Shmuel bar Naḥmani and names R. Yonatan as his teacher. Heilprin’s statement that Yuhasin omitted him may refer to a different witness.

Rosh Hashanah 34a gives Yishmael son of Yoḥanan ben Beroka in the baraita and Shmuel citing Yonatan in the subsequent discussion. Heilprin infers an early date, but citing both does not place the two sages in the same baraita.

Kohelet Rabbah names “the pupils of R. Abba” and Abba of Sidon. Midrash Shmuel names “the pupils of R. Immi” and Abba of Sidon. Both passages attribute a teaching to Shmuel. Heilprin’s wording brings both names into one compressed notice.
